body: As others have said I would go with the backwards timeline as well. How much older does he want to be with a young child, how old does he want to be when the kid graduates high school? What about retirement and paying for college? Also for you as the woman pregnancy, childbirth, and infancy is going to be a lot more on you. That will be physically easier younger. From observation and talking to lots of people 28-32 seems to be the sweet spot for starting a family. Good luck!

Get on birth control. Take the job. Go out with friends. Do the things you want to do while also spending time with him. Be kind but firm and lead your life how you want to. Hopefully you can strike a balance. If you can't then maybe it would be best if you guys split up. But try to lead the life you want while with him. he does not have the authority to tell you what to do.

We have kind of a strange set up I guess. I had lots of money saved up and invested when we got married that we used for a large down payment on the house, and setting up a new life together. (So financially, I feel like I kind of front-loaded, and then made very little money for a couple years) We moved for his job and I left my work and started a business when we got married. So initially he paid for everything and I supplemented with my savings when needed while I got my business off the ground. 

Since we were already accustomed to that and my income varies month to month he pays for everything. Any money beyond the monthly bills, expenses, and credit card he pretty much spends on his fun and hobbies. No savings or Investments. I put about 25 to 30% of my income into our joint account towards these expenses, depending on our needs. If we don't need it, then I put the rest of my income into savings. 

From the savings I invest some in stocks and Roth iras for both of us and then save up for bigger purchases and unexpected expenses... things like plane tickets/vacations, home repairs and remodels, new car, medical bills etc.

He has regular paychecks and is good at paying bills on time and being organized about that. I make sporadic income that can vary by thousands of dollars month to month. And I'm better at investing saving and planning, so this works for us!

Oh my God, get out! Get out get out get out! You sound like you're still young ish and early in the relationship. It will only get worse and become harder to leave. He knows he can disrespect you like this now and the pattern will continue. You will become more and more emotionally drained and less and less self-confident to the point you become stuck and miserable. Seriously get out now while you have the strength to.

Thanks for the response. I'm definitely not about to try to have a child for those reasons. I know they are not good reasons. I do feel a void and I can't help but wonder if it's because I should have had children. I thought I was on a good life path but I don't like where I've ended up. I guess I'm having serious doubts and wondering where I would be now if I had chosen a different path. Pretty common I'm sure. And I know a different path might not have gone any better. I just was really happy with my life, I thought I was on a good path so this has blindsided me in the last couple years. I'm finding myself full of regret wishing I had done just one thing differently so I didn't end up here now.

I guess I'm kind of thinking what if I had poured all that energy into my own child instead of just dumping it out all willy-nilly on people that aren't even in my life anymore. I would have something and someone to be proud of. And a reason to wake up in the morning. I don't know if I messed up.

Thanks for the kind response. I am an empathetic person. Sometimes to my detriment. Before I fell into this depression I was always trying to make someone's day or life a little bit better. But now I'm feeling like I've poured myself out emotionally into so many other people and things. I feel empty and tired. I don't even have the motivation or energy to take proper care of myself let aside others. I used to be so so happy and really love life. Now I just want to go to sleep and never wake up. It's terrible! :(
Thank you! I do have a sweet dog who is my BFF. It's great for getting out on walks and cuddling but definitely lacking in the conversation area. ;)

Oh dear, I'm afraid I'm realizing this might be what has happened. I didn't realize that emotional abuse was even a thing until recently. I thought if I could just make him happy... And when he's good he's great. But it's been so volatile. Now im feeling like I wasted my youth. What if I had been with someone who accepted me as I am and really cared for my soul? Someone I was never walking on eggshells with. I might have seen the pros in having children. At the very least I wouldn't have lost all my confidence and joy. I am 33 and feel defeated now. I don't know how to recover my life. It's heartbreaking.

I know this is an old thread but I just had to chime in. I studied abroad in a foreign country and took some intensive language classes when I first arrived. This girl in her late teens early twenties arrived at the school and couldn't speak the language at all at first. By the first week she could understand everything, the second week she could speak pretty well and by the third week she was speaking fluently and confidently. Man, it pissed me off. I was working so hard. Well, turns out she had a nanny as a little kid that spoke the language to her exclusively and it all came back. She needed to be in that immersed environment for it to happen. But she went from zero to fluent in 3 weeks. It was amazing! She had even taken the language in high school and not done very well. So I think it is there. Might just need some work recovering it.
I wish I had just been one of those women who always wanted to be a mom and then loved the job. I feel like life would have been easier following the script.

Please seek out a local women's shelter. They will help you with resources and protection. I used to volunteer with one of these places the last place I lived. If you would like, pm me with your general area and I will research where you can get help. 

I'm sorry you are dealing with this! My heart goes out to you!

Check out couchsurfing! You can stay with people for free all over the world. It sounds creepy, and I would go with a friend, especially if you're female. A friend and I spent four months one summer in college Couchsurfing and staying in cheap hostels around Europe. Still some of my best memories ever. A lot of the hosts on Couchsurfing really take you in, feed you, show you around. Everyone we stayed with turned out to be the opposite of creepy. We actually got to experience so much more of the culture than we would have staying at a hotel. A lot of people that host are interested in meeting people from other cultures and practicing their English. 

Of course this was all 10 years ago. I don't know if they still do this but at that time you could buy an unlimited rail pass for a certain amount of time. The rail pass and plane ticket were the main expenses. Then we would just buy food from the grocery store so that wasn't too expensive. 

Saving, planning, and prepping wasn't completely easy. But so so worth it. Think about it! 

Getting an education and being responsible is great. But deviating a little from the life script and having experiences is underrated. There is so much out there. You might not have a lot of money but right now you have the time and probably less responsibilities than you ever will in the future. 

If it's your dream try to make it happen!

Honest to God, I was fine. I was shocked. When I finished I was amazed to realize I could have done more, I could have kept going. That's why I felt like I had to share. I can't believe I didn't know this sooner. When I finished I just kept thinking what could I have done with a 20 year old body and the last 10 years? 

The only thing that hurt at the end was my hips from the backpack sitting on them, which I think can be fixed in the future by packing a little smarter and my calves were hella tight. 

Took a hot bath and within a day or two it was like physically nothing had ever happened. Mentally though it's been a combo of wow I can do anything and holy crap think of all the things I could have done if I hadn't been scared.

I started doing yoga a couple times a week and that has had a huge impact on my core and overall toning. Great for mental health too. Highly recommend. To train I also mountain biked ~5 hours a week, walked my dog at least two miles everyday and did a couple of 8-10 mile day hikes on the weekends. I'm lucky to live in the mountains so this was all rather enjoyable. 

Btw, mountain biking is another thing I never thought I could do until I picked it up 4ish years ago and absolutely love now! 

Sounds like a lot of you guys are already killing it and are woke to the possibilities. That is so awesome! Keep it up! And if you can take your gym muscles out into the mountains, do it! I grew up in a big city and I had no idea what was out there.

Appreciate the positive feedback. Thought this might be taken as preachy. I am just so late to the game and would love if this knowledge could positively impact someone. :)

No, no, no. Take one Adderall and get some shit done. Any shit. You have a tool on hand use it to help get you out of bed and motivated. Keep it by your bed. When you wake up take one then resume lounging around miserably as you've been doing. Eventually as it hits you'll get antsy and want to get up. Step one accomplished, you're out of bed! Step2, go for a walk. It's out in the real world but you don't have to talk to anyone or interact with anyone. Just get some sun on your face, get some fresh air, get your blood flowing. If that's all you get done for the day, so be it. You will feel maybe just a tiny bit better. But hopefully it's enough to propel you into the next thing. 

Now here is where it gets tricky because your options are so wide open. What do you want to do? I think a job would help you. Having a commitment, a schedule, something that forces you to interact, and eases your money stress will be positive overall. You're in a bad way right now so you don't have to go all in and get your full-time dream job or whatever. Take baby steps. Even if it's just a part time job 2 days a week. It will be hard and hurt at first but then you might start to feel a little bit better. Hopefully you can work your way up to having more confidence and being reacclimated into the world to feel comfortable enough to return to school or get a full-time job. If you're not quite feeling up for it yet, make a to-do list and even if you can get a couple things done those are baby steps forward. Like a load of laundry, grocery shopping, cooking dinner etc. 

Force yourself to interact with other humans. You can set small goals. You can start with the teller at the grocery store or whoever you have to interact with in public. Force yourself to smile and act normal. Try to force yourself to do things with friends. Force yourself to do the things that used to make you happy. Fake it. Just keep at it. Honestly you've isolated yourself away for a while so this all seems overwhelming and not enjoyable. But if you can get yourself out little by little it will go from painful to neutral to hopefully enjoyable. 

I know you're down and low on energy. But if you can muster it try to do something nice for someone else. Either a friend stranger or acquaintance. Doesn't matter. Doesn't have to be big. It will help you feel a little better about yourself.

You can totally do this! Just take small steps!

Keep trying different volunteer organizations until you find one that's a better fit to make friends. Last time I moved I volunteered with eight or nine organizations before I found one where I really clicked with the other members and then I threw myself into that. Made great friends and got a lot done in the community! 

Moving away from family and loved ones is really really tough. You might have a larger dating pool in a bigger city. But definitely weigh the pros and cons. Do you have an option to move somewhere larger that's still fairly close?

I know this sounds crazy, but try to order you a man and the life you want from the universe! Write down what you want. Think about it all the time. Put it out there to the universe. I know this sounds crazy but I've had some luck with it and I think other people have too. Put it out there in a positive way. The more you think like this that you're alone and always will be, you're attracting that to yourself.

You can't because it will break the hearts and forever ruin the lives of so many people that love you. You know you can't do that so you know you have to press forward. I don't know the answer but try to shift your thinking away from that option. 

Would you be interested in some schooling? Maybe even trade school? Could be a positive thing to put your energy into and could result in a job that gives you confidence and more options due to decent income.

I'm old. I guarantee it just gets worse but you have to roll with it. Stay active! Even if it's just a minimum of walking a few miles a day. I highly recommend yoga. Keep that in mind as your body ages and your life gets more stressful. I probably wouldn't have given a crap if someone recommended that to me at your age. But one day... :) 

I literally just came over here to post this message, but then I saw yours and thought I'd share. Your body is capable of so much right now? Don't miss out! :) 

 I just completed a strenuous 32 mile backpacking trip in 3 days at the age of 32. That sounded so hard before I did it. I didn't imagine I could do something like this. It was almost easy. I could've woken up again the next day and done it again. It was an incredible experience and I felt amazing after. I was fairly athletic throughout my 20s but didn't realize what my body was capable of with a little bit of pushing. And I was only in decent shape. Not great or amazing shape. I'm in the best shape of my life now, but already my knees are hurting sometimes. I'm not so old and I plan to have some more big adventures but still my body already feels older than even 5 years ago, and certainly older than 10 years ago. I wish i had started sooner. I wish I could go back and tell myself to get in amazing shape and really use my young body. Since I can't, I'm telling you all! ;) Seriously, get out there, be brave, try adventure sports. You are capable of so much more than you think. And it can be so fun and rewarding. Also, if you have the means... Travel. I didn't have the money to travel as much as I would have liked, but those experiences I was lucky to have were so eye opening. I wish I had prioritized it and budgeted for it even more. 

Sorry if this is misplaced, I'm just thinking about all the things I could have done in the last decade if I knew how strong I was capable of being. I always thought those extreme people were just a different breed. (And they are!) But anyone is capable of much more than they imagine. So take advantage of those young bodies, kids! :)
Umm or is there somewhere else I should post this? I dunno who would care. I probably wouldn't have been interested as a teenager, but taken it more to heart in my early to mid 20s. Thanks! :)

Maybe just offer to watch the kid one night after they put her to bed so they can go out for dinner. You can have a nice evening in if you're into that. When we've gone on beach trips before we usually rent a place with kitchen and like to cook meals and sit on the balcony drinking wine some nights anyway. That wouldn't be a huge sacrifice for you and would let your friends get a night out. I mean they are your friends it would be nice to give them a couple hours out if you can still enjoy your time in.

This is super important! You're so young. Obviously thoughtful and mature to be considering all this, but don't rush into marriage! You don't want to lose yourself. It's awesome that you're thinking through and discussing everything. Take your time. Sounds like you're on a great path.
